question: Which plant is considered a noxious weed that has a chemical defence mechanism to protect it from predators?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Calotropis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Calotropis:-**

 
 
• **It is a genus of flowering plants in the family Apocynaceae.**
 
• It was first described as a genus in 1810.
 
• It is native to southern Asia and North Africa.
 
• They are commonly known as milkweeds because of the latex they produce.
 
• They are large shrubs growing to 4 m (13 ft) tall.
 
• **It is considered a noxious weed that has a chemical defence mechanism to protect it from predators**
 
 
 
• [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/17f4cb6618058e795dceecc3ca73e6bc53c96a6ca899666c7e8d766254e39f06.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chicory:-**

 
 
• It is scientifically known as Cichorium intybus.
 
• It is a somewhat woody, perennial herbaceous plant that usually has bright blue flowers.
 
• It originates from Europe and is now also found in North America and Australia.
 
• It's often seen growing along roadsides and in open fields.
 
• The plant is known for its long taproot, which is often ground into a powder and used as a coffee substitute or coffee additive.
 
 
 
• **Black henbane:-**
 
 
• It is scientifically known as Hyoscyamus niger, is a plant that originates from Eurasia.
 
• It's part of the nightshade family, which includes both poisonous and nonpoisonous plants such as tomatoes, potatoes, and belladonna.
 
• It's a biennial or short-lived perennial plant, with a strong, unpleasant odor.
 
 
 
• **Field bindweed:-**
 
 
• It is scientifically named Convolvulus arvensis, is a plant from the morning glory family.
 
• It is mostly perennial and native to Europe and Asia but has become widely distributed worldwide.
 
• It's known for being robust and difficult to control, characteristics that have made it quite problematic in agricultural settings where it is considered a significant weed.
